decontamination_notes: Real bug fix from toml-rs/toml PR #1194 (closes #440), merged 2026-07-28, after the training cutoffs of the models this suite targets; re-check upstream_merged against any newer model's cutoff before reusing. toml::value::Datetime asks serde for TOML's private datetime struct; the legacy toml::Value deserializer forwarded deserialize_struct to deserialize_any, where Value::Datetime is represented as a string, so typed conversions from an already-parsed Value or Table failed with a type error while the direct parser path worked. The fix handles the private datetime struct in Value's deserialize_struct, forwards Table's deserialize_struct to the Value implementation, and deliberately leaves deserialize_any unchanged so generic cross-format conversions (e.g. into serde_json::Value) still produce a string. Workspace sliced at the PR base commit (4ec099fe) with cargo-prune to the dependency closure of the toml crate (toml, toml_datetime, toml_parser, toml_writer, serde_spanned; crates/ layout preserved), third-party deps vendored (Cargo.lock regenerated for the pruned workspace, cargo vendor + .cargo/config.toml) so the sandbox builds offline; MIT/Apache LICENSEs preserved. Coverage: 4 fail_to_pass tests, each verified failing at base and passing after the gold patch (typed Datetime from Value, all four datetime flavors, a Datetime struct field from Table, and from Value); 3 pass_to_pass guards pin the deserialize_any string representation for JSON conversion, the direct-from-document parser path, and plain typed Table fields. Assertions check parsed values via public APIs, never error text. Image is vulcanbench/sandbox:rust-2024 (rustc 1.90): the regenerated lockfile pulls dev-deps (e.g. the ignore crate) that use let-chains, which need rustc >= 1.88 — the 1.87 :rust image cannot build them.
